goals: mechanistic: quantify historical baseline recharge and its sensitivity to the basin's climate (elevation) and soil gradients
projection (as-posed): estimate recharge change by 2050 under warming — NOT answerable with current forcing
validation: compare modeled recharge/WTD to observations — no in-domain data
drivers_to_resolve: climate (via elevation gradient in NLDAS forcing)

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM resolves snow, soil moisture, and sub-surface drainage/recharge; elevation-resolved NLDAS makes climate a meaningful stratifier across 1625 m of relief.

answerable: historical (1980-2018) baseline recharge magnitude and seasonality per column
sensitivity of recharge to the elevation-driven climate gradient (rain vs snow, melt timing) via NLDAS
sensitivity of recharge to soil texture (SSURGO)
a time-for-time analog: recharge in warm/dry vs cool/wet historical years (bounds sensitivity, NOT a scenario)

not_answerable.aspect: projection of recharge to 2050 under a warming scenario
not_answerable.why: forcing is NLDAS-2 historical only (1980-2018); the runs' only forcing lever is choice of historical years — there is no future-climate forcing and no capability to impose a warming delta on the forcing

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation climate-bands x 2 dominant soil classes = 6 combinations; x2 light replication to capture within-stratum forcing/soil spread = 12. Smallest set that spans the climate gradient AND the recharge-controlling soil contrast.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns in the rain-snow transition band where melt-timing shifts most strongly modulate recharge, and in valley bottoms where drainage/storage is largest; ridgetops sampled sparsely (12 km cells under-resolve peak SWE there).
sampling_strategy.replication: x2 per stratum to expose the spread of NLDAS cell forcing and SSURGO soil within each band.

sampling_plan.reason: baseline high-drainage recharge where precip is rain, not snow
isolates soil-texture throttle on recharge under rain forcing
melt-timing-sensitive recharge, the band most responsive to warming — key climate-sensitivity signal
melt timing x low-drainage interaction in the transition zone
snowmelt-driven recharge pulse; upper bound of climate control
snow-fed recharge under low-drainage soil; ridgetop SWE caveat noted

validation_design.comparison: none — validation gap; only physical-expectation / literature plausibility checks possible

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline NLDAS historical forcing, native SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start

requires_capabilities.capability: future-climate / delta-perturbed forcing (CMIP/SSP downscaled or a ΔT/precip-scaling forcing modifier)
requires_capabilities.why: the question asks for a 2050 warming scenario; historical NLDAS cannot represent a future forced climate
requires_capabilities.blocks: the entire projection — the primary question as posed

requires_capabilities.capability: model spin-up OR Fan-2013 WTD-informed warm start
requires_capabilities.why: recharge and water table are slow states; cold-start at default 8.8 m gives recharge~0 artifacts
recharge timing in this basin is melt-controlled
requires_capabilities.blocks: attributing recharge changes to snow-vs-rain shifts

requires_capabilities.why: to place columns into the three elevation climate-bands
no observations currently available in Naches

assumptions: NLDAS-2 (CONUS) covers the Naches bbox so per-column forcing is elevation-resolved.
Naches recharge is snow-influenced, so melt timing is a first-order control (basis for the rain-snow transition emphasis).
SSURGO provides usable dominant soil classes across the basin.
The warm/cool historical-year analog is treated strictly as a sensitivity bound, not a 2050 projection.
open_questions: Which future scenario (SSP/RCP) and downscaling product should drive the projection once future forcing is available?
Is a time-for-time analog (warm/dry vs cool/wet historical years) an acceptable interim sensitivity product for the user?
Are there any recharge, streamflow-baseflow, or well/WTD observations for Naches (USGS, state) that could be ingested to close the validation gap?
Should spin-up length or Fan-2013 warm start be used given cost vs. accuracy for the recharge target?
